messages.subject: web design
parts:
I am trying to use the Program DISTANCE to estimate population
densities of nocturnal rodents (mice and voles) in four vegetation
communities in the Southern Rocky Mountains. I am inheriting a web
design following Parmenter et al., 2003 and using the Program DISTANCE
to estimate density. We have caught mice and voles 4 consecutive
nights during a trapping session (mark/recapture). We have 3 trapping
sessions to look for temporal changes. I am looking for a couple of
insights into the Properties by which to enter the data. I enter the
data in a point-center model and as clusters of first captures for a
trapping session. I am pretty sure this is appropriate. However, I am
not sure how to enter "no captures" in a particular ring for a
particular trapping session. In the program it can be entered as 0
(in which it calculates a density that averages 0 into cluster sizes)
or -1 (in which a "no capture " ring is not used to average cluster
size in the analysis. Using one approach or the other gives very
different numbers.

Has anyone used this trapping design and program and has advice on teh
best way to proceed? Thanks for your help.

Thanks,
Barry Rosenbaum
